posts.note: Personal essay about a Rupert Neve 5088 mixing console frame in a crate; only personal plans and an aside about a pending lawsuit.
Podcast blurb; the RAMHT 2026 event announcement supplies the forward-looking items.
Annotated read of a DOJ press release on a new indictment of Done Global and Mindful Mental Wellness. Quoted DOJ text ('If convicted, Done Global faces...') was not logged as the author's claim.

Essay on New York's new MAiD law. The title itself ('Will Be Used to Kill The Mentally Ill') is a forecast but is not in the cached body text; body equivalents were logged. Five 'We should exclude...' recommendations are normative and were not logged.
Sales-tips listicle; mostly advice. RAMHT promo plus a footnote forecast about the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2021.
Satirical Polar Express parody framed as a deposition (Epstein-files allusion). Two fiction-framed items logged with sincere=false.
Holiday anthology of links; RAMHT announcement, a tongue-in-cheek Prime Day claim, and a conditional commitment to keep writing.

Explicit 2026 predictions list (items 1-12 plus a bonus). Also restatements of earlier calls (ERISA enforcement, 'Every Employer Will Be Sued', MDMA-AT non-approval) and one quoted third-party forecast about Schlichter suits.
Adolescent antidepressant essay; 'should' recommendations not logged. Two forecasts (litigation, payer coverage) plus RAMHT items.
RAMHT-AI speaker preview; several hedged expectations about announcements by speakers' companies (GrayMatters, Beckley Clinical, NRx/Hope) and one about Psyrin/Radial vocal biomarker technology.
Podcast blurb; only the RAMHT reminder.

statements.quote: I’m going to build a studio around it, and I’m likely to be unsettled still. I know it won’t solve any real problem.
statements.context: Personal essay about a Rupert Neve Designs 5088 recording console frame that has sat in a 1178-pound crate for years after moves, a pandemic, a business exit and a lawsuit. The author plans to build a home studio around the console and expects it will not resolve his restlessness.
statements.note: Personal plan; low forecast value.

statements.quote: I will still be who I am. But, someday soon, with a few dB lower noise floor.
statements.context: Closing line of the console essay: the author expects to have the console commissioned and a working studio 'someday soon'.
statements.note: Personal plan; low forecast value.

statements.quote: a lawsuit —yet to be fully adjudicated, despite the manifest facts and meritorious legal arguments to be brought, with aplomb, to the doorstep of Plainfitts and Counterclaimants
statements.context: Aside listing the adverse events that delayed the console installation, including a pending lawsuit. Footnote 1 names the other parties as Amanda Itzkoff, M.D., Jack Aron Wolcowitz and associated parties. The author expects meritorious legal arguments to be brought against them.
statements.note: Implied expectation about a pending lawsuit involving the author; borderline. CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: Announcing: Rapid-Acting Mental Health Treatment (RAMHT) Returns January 11th in San Francisco.
statements.context: Event announcement appended to a podcast post about AI chatbots as relationship advisors. RAMHT 2026, the author's live newsletter event, is scheduled for January 11, 2026 in San Francisco; listed sponsors and speakers include MdHub.ai, Simple Practice, Radial, AtaiBeckley, Attentio.ai, Emobot, Hope Theraputics, Psyrin.ai, GrayMatters Health and Ampa.
statements.note: Own-event announcement; coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: And a few more to be announced soon! It will be off the hook, as usual.
statements.context: Follows the RAMHT 2026 sponsor and speaker list. The author expects additional sponsors or speakers to be announced soon and predicts the event will be a success.
statements.note: Own-event promotion; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: Unless it’s a health plan, in which case we will let it slide— as UHG did 7 days ago.
statements.context: Annotated read of the DOJ press release on a new indictment of Done Global and Mindful Mental Wellness P.A. Reacting to HHS-OIG's line about exploiting federal programs, the author sarcastically predicts that health plans (citing UnitedHealth Group a week earlier) will not face the same enforcement.
statements.note: Sarcastic phrasing; the underlying expectation (health plans escape enforcement) reads as sincere.

statements.quote: So this case will be about the books. Thanks DOJ! Tax fraud is a real crime, and it is easy to prove if you have already completed discovery in the first case.
statements.context: After the IRS Criminal Investigation quote in the DOJ press release, the author predicts the new Done Global / MMW case will center on financial records and be easy to prove given discovery from the first case against Ruthia He and David Brody.
statements.note: Legal-process forecast.

statements.quote: Every DEA license involved could be pulled. Let’s see some real consequences, DOJ.
statements.context: After noting that Done Global founder Ruthia He and clinical president David Brody were previously convicted, the author says the DEA registrations of everyone involved in the Done/Mindful prescribing could be revoked.
statements.note: Hedged possibility followed by a wish.

statements.quote: Now, “how short” a video will matter. But this sets a standard. Other virtual care providers are watching closely.
statements.context: Commenting on the indictment's allegation that Done prescribed based on short video or audio contact or none at all. The author predicts the length of telehealth contact will become a legal standard that other virtual care providers must meet.
statements.note: Standard-setting forecast for telehealth prescribing.

statements.quote: It’s not the crime, it’s the cover-up. And it’s a lot of cover-up, I’ll bet.
statements.context: On the allegation that Done Global conspired to alter, destroy and conceal records after a grand jury subpoena. The author bets extensive record destruction will be shown.
statements.note: Expectation about what the case will reveal.

statements.quote: PRISON TIME, and financial ruin. With interest. Nothing else will even remotely discourage capital from flowing to nitwits like this in the future.
statements.context: Soapbox on penalties: the maximum penalty of twice the gross profits is called inadequate (the Sacklers cited as still wealthy). The author asserts that only prison time and financial ruin will deter investors from funding schemes like Done in the future.
statements.note: Mixed normative/predictive claim: capital will keep flowing to such ventures unless penalties are severe.

statements.quote: I have limited faith that state medical boards will do much here—they move too slowly, especially in California.
statements.context: Reacting to the press release's note that CMS and HHS-OIG are taking steps to hold providers accountable. The author doubts state medical boards, particularly California's, will act meaningfully against the prescribers involved.

statements.quote: And yet, given the “already convicted” founders, I doubt this will go that far south. But due process is due to all, even and especially the guilty.
statements.context: Reacting to the DOJ boilerplate that an indictment is merely an allegation and defendants are presumed innocent. The author expects the case against Done Global and MMW will not collapse, given the founders' prior convictions.
statements.note: Legal outcome forecast.

statements.quote: Yes, you insurance company will have plenty of in network stimulant prescribers handy…Except, I doubt they will.
statements.context: On the DOJ's guidance that displaced Done patients should contact their insurer to find a new provider. The author predicts insurers will not have enough in-network stimulant prescribers for these patients.
statements.note: First sentence is sarcastic; the second states the real expectation.

statements.quote: Many adults will still have ADHD, and will need treatment.
statements.context: 'Pro Tip' that removing 40 million pills of supply requires a collaborative care bonus payment model to handle the fallout. The author predicts continuing treatment need among adults displaced from Done.
statements.note: Near-truism; logged for recall.

statements.quote: This will similarly go well… oh, wait.
statements.context: Sarcastic reaction to the DOJ's crisis-support guidance directing displaced patients to the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. The author's meaning is that this redirection will not go well.
statements.note: Sarcasm: literal words are the opposite of the intended expectation.

statements.quote: This leaves the door wide open to chronically suicidal individuals, for whom psychiatric medications haven't helped. Many of those individuals will have personality disorders, for which suicidality is a common symptom.
statements.context: Essay titled 'New York's New Medically Assisted Aid In Dying Law Will Be Used to Kill The Mentally Ill'. After quoting the NY law's definition of terminal illness, the author predicts chronically suicidal patients, many with personality disorders, will qualify for and use MAiD in New York.
entities: NY Medical Aid in Dying Act
statements.note: Body-text equivalent of the title's forecast.

statements.quote: This is always intended to be used only in extreme cases; more people are terminally ill, and then it expands to others whose suffering is tremendous, but not terminal in the traditional sense of the term. That's what happens in the real world.
statements.context: The author grants the NY law's intent is narrow but asserts a general pattern: MAiD starts with the terminally ill and expands to non-terminal suffering. Applied to New York as an implicit forecast of expansion.
statements.note: Generalization from other jurisdictions with a predictive reading for NY.

statements.quote: However, I suspect there will be a problem, and I'm going to use some data to back it up. It always starts carefully, restricted, and framed as rare . Then, it ramps up.
statements.context: After comparing NY's criteria (more restrictive now) with Canada's 2016 criteria, the author predicts MAiD use in New York will ramp up over time, citing Dutch and Canadian numbers.

statements.quote: Dear readers, I want you to imagine the hundreds of people who are going to apply for assistance, and try, beg, insist to their doctors that they can't live for another six months.
statements.context: After presenting the Dutch cohort of young psychiatric MAiD applicants, the author predicts hundreds of chronically suicidal patients will apply for aid in dying under the NY law.
statements.note: Numeric-ish: 'hundreds'.

statements.quote: More people are gonna die by their own choosing if they don't have to do it for themselves, and maybe that's more humane. It's probably more humane for some, and more lethal for others.
statements.context: The author predicts that MAiD availability will increase deaths by choice, more humane for some and more lethal for others.

statements.quote: We're not saying out loud the quiet part—we're gonna consign, traumatized women with autism, personality disorders, depression, and other forms of psychological suffering that, overwhelmingly, we as a society have chosen to inflict upon them, well, while not holding the perpetrators accountable.
statements.context: The author predicts the NY MAiD law will consign traumatized young women with psychiatric conditions to death while society avoids an honest conversation about the trade-off.

statements.quote: We indemnify those who assist in death, in this law, and for those who champion life? Medical malpractice claims await.
statements.context: Contrasting legal indemnity for MAiD providers under the NY law with malpractice exposure for physicians who try to prevent suicide in high-risk patients. The author predicts continued malpractice claims for the latter.

statements.quote: This will end as poorly as it has in every other place it's been implemented. It may be a decision, a series of trade-offs, we're comfortable with, but we haven't been frank enough with ourselves to have that conversation.
statements.context: Central forecast of the essay: New York's MAiD law will produce the same outcomes as the Netherlands and Canada (use by psychiatric patients, rising numbers, deaths of vulnerable young people).
statements.note: Core claim of the post.

statements.quote: Adding MAiD to the roster increases the rate of individuals who die in their youth.
statements.context: After the Dutch cohort data (4.3% died by suicide during the application process, 3% by MAiD) against a roughly 5% base rate of suicide in borderline personality disorder, the author asserts that MAiD for psychiatric suffering raises youth deaths.
statements.note: General causal claim in present tense; predictive reading for NY is implicit. Borderline.

statements.quote: Say it with me: Broad insurance coverage for life-saving psychiatric treatment now, please. At a bare minimum, it will reduce the spending on physician suicide assessments.
statements.context: Closing recommendation after a list of proposed exclusions for the NY law. Conditional forecast: broad insurance coverage of treatments for suicidality (TMS, ketamine, DBT, etc.) would reduce spending on physician suicide and MAiD assessments.
statements.note: Conditional on coverage being adopted; partly normative.

statements.quote: Promotional Message : Our live action newsletter event is happening soon! Rapid-Acting Mental Health Treatment (RAMHT) Returns January 11th in San Francisco.
statements.context: Promotional block in a sales-tips article for healthcare start-ups. RAMHT 2026 (the author's live event) is scheduled for January 11, 2026 in San Francisco with sponsors MdHub.ai, Simple Practice, Radial, AtaiBeckley, Attentio.ai, Emobot, Hope Theraputics, Psyrin.ai, GrayMatters Health and Ampa.
statements.note: Own-event announcement; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: It will be off the hook, as usual. I know, a live action Newsletter Event. For those looking for a discount, just message me.
statements.context: Continuation of the RAMHT 2026 promotional block; the author predicts the event will be a success.
statements.note: Own-event promotion; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: So if you have venture money and you want to sell a thing that saves money or works better—self-funded employers + dual-eligible Medicare/Medicaid populations are the only ones who will have aligned incentives. Thus savings plays take more capital to get to scale, not less.
statements.context: Sales tip 1 ('It Needs to Work') for health-tech founders. The author asserts that only self-funded employers and dual-eligible Medicare/Medicaid populations will have incentives aligned with cost-saving products, so savings-based companies need more capital to scale.
statements.note: Market generalization with a predictive reading; borderline.

statements.quote: This is thanks to the combined appropriations act of 2021, which is going to create a Sea Change in healthcare. You heard it here first, or you already know me and you've heard me talk about this for years and want me to just shut up about it already.
statements.context: Footnote 2, attached to the point that brokers must now disclose all payments and act as fiduciaries. The author predicts the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2021 (broker compensation disclosure, gag clause and fiduciary provisions) will create a sea change in healthcare.
statements.note: Restatement of a long-held call ('talk about this for years').

statements.quote: We climbed mountains so high it seemed as if we would scrape the moon, like that 3I/ATLAS is about to!
statements.context: Satirical Polar Express parody framed as a deposition transcript. An aside claims the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS is about to scrape the moon.
statements.note: Joke inside fiction; not a real expectation.

statements.quote: No wonder Santa was afraid for his life . But maybe, just maybe, justice can now be done.
statements.context: Ending of the parody: a silver bell from Santa opens to reveal a USB key with hundreds of thousands of unredacted documents, an allusion to the redacted Epstein files. The narrator hopes justice can now be done.
statements.note: Fictional frame with a magical premise; a hope rather than a forecast.

statements.quote: Let’s not forget that, after the holidays, comes the New Year, and with it, the Rapid-Acting Mental Health Treatment event in San Francisco—coming up on January 11th, 2026!
statements.context: Holiday anthology of past satirical posts; announces the RAMHT 2026 event in San Francisco on January 11, 2026.
statements.note: Own-event announcement; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: this gem about Prime Day, which is on track to overtake Christmas in the next few years
statements.context: In a list of past holiday posts, the author describes a premium article claiming Amazon Prime Day is on track to overtake Christmas within a few years. The anthology is explicitly of 'silly posts'.
statements.note: Tongue-in-cheek; the literal claim does not read as a real expectation.

statements.quote: if you keep subscribing, sharing, and commenting, I’ll keep writing.
statements.context: Closing line of the holiday anthology; conditional commitment to keep writing The Frontier Psychiatrists.
statements.note: Own commitment about the newsletter; low forecast value. CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: This is only the first shot. ERISA is next. The department of labor has already weighed in last week in the state of Massachusetts on fiduciary violations under that statute. Enforcement is coming. This is not a drill.
statements.context: Opening of the 2026 predictions post: the author quotes his own very first article (about a DOJ EMTALA suit against Ohio) to show his track record. The restated call is that ERISA fiduciary enforcement against employers over health plans is coming.
statements.note: Restatement of an earlier call (from the author's first article), presented as vindicated by recent ERISA suits.

statements.quote: Then I wrote the following in 2024: Every Employer Will Be Sued...Personally
statements.context: Restated 2024 headline prediction that every employer will be sued personally for ERISA fiduciary breaches over health plans. The author notes a batch of such suits (Schlichter Bogard against United Airlines, CHS, Universal Services of America, LabCorp and benefits consultants) was filed the prior week.
statements.note: Restatement of a 2024 call; author adds 'I didn't imagine it would be all at once'.

statements.quote: It was a classic Schlichter litigation “dump” with suits filed against multiple employers alleging similar violations all on the same day (and, if prior history holds true, this won’t be the last batch).
statements.context: Quoted excerpt (with a footnote marker) from a third-party report headlined 'Schlichter Bogard Unleashes a New ERISA Suit Genre', covering suits against United Airlines, CHS/Community Health Systems, Universal Services of America and Laboratory Corp. of America, plus consultants Gallagher, Mercer, Lockton and Willis Towers Watson. The excerpt predicts more batches of suits.
statements.note: Quoted third-party text; the author includes it approvingly but does not explicitly adopt it.

statements.quote: I also predicted the FDA would not approve MDMA-AT. I provided a whole series of arguments in support of that viewpoint.
statements.context: Track-record section of the 2026 predictions post; the author restates his earlier prediction that the FDA would not approve MDMA-assisted therapy and links his seven-part series on saving MDMA-AT.
statements.note: Restatement of a past call cited as track record, not a new forecast; the text presents it as already resolved.

statements.quote: Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment (RAMHT-AI) is coming! Live, and in person . ... January 11th, in San Fran—right in the middle of JPM Health.
statements.context: Advertisement block inside the 2026 predictions post: RAMHT-AI, the author's live event, is scheduled for January 11, 2026 in San Francisco during JPM Healthcare week, with a free ticket code.
statements.note: Own-event announcement; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: The first ERISA lawsuit referencing mental health parity violations will be filed. ... I have been arguing that this is a good case to bring. It happens in 2026.
statements.context: Item 1 of 'The Frontier Psychiatrists' 2026 predictions': the first ERISA fiduciary lawsuit citing mental health parity (MHPAEA) violations will be filed in 2026.

statements.quote: AI-Powered Neuromodulation becomes the hot new Venture Funding category.
statements.context: Item 2 of the 2026 predictions list: AI-powered neuromodulation becomes the hot venture funding category in 2026.
statements.note: Flat assertion under the 2026 predictions heading.

statements.quote: I think 2026 doubles that number into AI-enabled BCI companies, and we will see additional dollars and deal flow into non-invasive devices, too.
statements.context: Item 3 of the 2026 predictions list. Setup: 2025 saw over $300m invested in neuromodulation health-tech companies (Radial, Beckley Clinical, Stella Centers, NRx subsidiary Hope Theraputics, plus Big Leap, Osmind's pivot, Everbright). The author predicts 2026 investment doubles (over $600m) into AI-enabled BCI companies with more deal flow into non-invasive devices.
statements.note: Numeric: doubling of >$300m. Radial is the author's employer; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: Look out for news from Merge Labs , Neuralink , and expect Jeff Bezos and maybe even Zuck to have invested in a company in the space.
statements.context: Item 4 of the 2026 predictions list (BCI/neuromodulation): news from Merge Labs and Neuralink, and investments by Jeff Bezos and possibly Mark Zuckerberg in a company in the space during 2026.
statements.note: Compound claim: Merge Labs/Neuralink news; Bezos invests; Zuckerberg maybe invests.

statements.quote: Top-lines from Sanmai, Brainsonix, and other tFUS companies are likely to make news too.
statements.context: Item 4 of the 2026 predictions list, continued: top-line results from transcranial focused ultrasound companies Sanmai, Brainsonix and others will make news in 2026.

statements.quote: Large-scale trials of Neuromodulation for non-psychiatric indications will start enrolling. Expect Parkinson’s Disease, dystonia, TD, weight loss, and pain associated with general medical conditions to enroll, if not conclude enrollment.
statements.context: Item 5 of the 2026 predictions list: large neuromodulation trials in non-psychiatric indications (Parkinson's disease, dystonia, tardive dyskinesia, weight loss, pain in general medical conditions) will begin enrolling in 2026.

statements.quote: We will have insurance coverage by a national payor—or two—or Accelerated TMS—in the outpatient clinic setting in 2026. It won’t be broad—it will start with pilots and narrow network deals, but the chips will begin to fall.
statements.context: Item 6 of the 2026 predictions list: one or two national payers will cover accelerated TMS in outpatient clinics in 2026, starting with pilots and narrow network deals. Accompanied by a photo caption about training on the Ampa system at what was Fermata, before Radial.
statements.note: 'or Accelerated TMS' reads as a typo for 'for'. Radial (author's employer) delivers accelerated TMS; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: There will be three or more at-home depression treatment devices on the market by the end of 2026. We already have the Flow approval announced, and more is coming.
statements.context: Item 7 of the 2026 predictions list: at least three at-home depression treatment devices on the (US) market by end of 2026; Flow Neuroscience's approval is cited as already announced.
statements.note: Numeric: three or more devices.

statements.quote: A ntidepressant prescriptions will drop (globally) for the first time in 2026. This is an ambitious prediction, but I think the zeitgeist and the data are both against these small-molecule drugs.
statements.context: Item 8 of the 2026 predictions list: global antidepressant prescriptions fall for the first time in 2026.
statements.note: Typo 'A ntidepressant' preserved verbatim from the source.

statements.quote: A professional society for kids’ care (AAP, AACAP, or the like) will issue a warning (or stern guideline) against prescribing all drugs (except prozac) for depression in youth.
statements.context: Item 9 of the 2026 predictions list: a pediatric or child psychiatry professional society (AAP, AACAP or similar) will issue a warning or guideline against prescribing antidepressants other than fluoxetine for youth depression.

statements.quote: COMP360 and KetaFree (IV Ketamine) will be approved for MDD by FDA.
statements.context: Item 10 of the 2026 predictions list: FDA approval in 2026 of Compass Pathways' COMP360 (psilocybin) and NRx's KetaFree (IV ketamine) for major depressive disorder.
statements.note: Compound claim: two separate FDA approvals (COMP360; KetaFree IV ketamine).

statements.quote: At least two pandemic-era mental-health companies will publicly cease operations— I’m looking at you, fictional DeathStance Health .
statements.context: Item 11 of the 2026 predictions list: at least two pandemic-era mental health companies publicly shut down in 2026. 'DeathStance Health' is a fictional stand-in name.
statements.note: Numeric: at least two companies. The named company is explicitly fictional.

statements.quote: There will be an additional 2-3 major criminal cases brought against companies selling controlled substances. Done will be convicted all over again .
statements.context: Item 11 of the 2026 predictions list, continued: two to three more major criminal cases against companies selling controlled substances in 2026, and Done Global convicted again in its new indictment.
statements.note: Compound claim: 2-3 new criminal cases; Done convicted again. Legal/enforcement area.

statements.quote: Everything will be okay enough for most, and the world won’t (literally) end. Hard times will continue for many.
statements.context: Item 12 of the 2026 predictions list: a broad statement that the world will not end in 2026 and hard times will continue for many.
statements.note: Broad, hard to resolve.

statements.quote: And as a bonus…a long shot, but I’m going to put my dime down. ... Alien life will make contact , and we will know we are not alone
statements.context: Bonus item after the 2026 predictions list: the author bets, as a self-described long shot, that alien life makes contact in 2026.
statements.note: Playful long-shot framed as a real bet; coder may judge sincerity.

statements.quote: Any family with a bad outcome— there are 700,000 suicide attempts among adolescents in 2024 —can and will start suing and winning. The last prescriber in holding the hot-potato, and who who didn’t document a plan for deprescribing? I wouldn’t want to be an underwriter.
statements.context: First of four recommendations in an essay on the lack of efficacy of non-fluoxetine oral antidepressants in adolescents (9.44M such prescriptions in 2022). The author predicts families will sue prescribers of these drugs after bad outcomes and win, creating liability for the last prescriber.
statements.note: Litigation forecast tied to a deprescribing recommendation.

statements.quote: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation has an FDA label for adolescent depression, and national coverage from UnitedHealthgroup, Cigna, Medical, and more for heaven’s sake. Other plans will follow.
statements.context: Second recommendation: TMS for adolescent depression is FDA-labeled and nationally covered by UnitedHealth Group and Cigna; the author predicts other health plans will follow with coverage.
statements.note: Radial (author's employer) delivers TMS; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: RAMHT-AI 2026 Happens Sunday, January 11th!
statements.context: Event block: RAMHT-AI 2026, the author's fifth live newsletter event, takes place Sunday January 11, 2026 in San Francisco before JPM, with a free ticket code and a program listing speakers from Radial, Neurolief, Attentio, SimplePractice, GrayMatters Health, MDHub, Psyrin, Emobot, Ampa Health, NRx, AtaiBeckley and Beckley Clinical.
statements.note: Own-event announcement; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: Companies have been dreamed up at RAMHT, patients have learned of hope, products have be announced, science has been unveiled, and more excitement is in store this year too.
statements.context: Closing of the RAMHT-AI 2026 program section; the author predicts announcements and excitement at this year's event.
statements.note: Own-event promotion; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: This Sunday, we are throwing the fifth Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment event, this time incorporating our long-standing belief that AI is part of the future, in the name of the event: RAMHT-AI.
statements.context: Preview post for RAMHT-AI, the author's fifth live event, on Sunday January 11, 2026 in San Francisco.
statements.note: Own-event announcement; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: Now, there's a clinical trial in the works, and his product, Emobot, is already tracking the moods of thousands of people—passively, throughout their day!
statements.context: Example of RAMHT connections leading to real changes: the author met Tanel Petelot (Emobot) at a prior RAMHT; a clinical trial of Emobot's passive mood tracking is now planned.
statements.note: Status statement implying a future trial; borderline.

statements.quote: But, they're probably gonna have something new to tell us that even I don't know about, and I'm really excited to hear what they have next.
statements.context: Speaker preview for Kirk Thelander, CCO of GrayMatters Health (PRISM EEG neurofeedback; PTSD treatment and an emerging anhedonia/MDD treatment). The author expects GrayMatters to announce something new at RAMHT-AI.
statements.note: Expectation about an event announcement; low stakes.

statements.quote: NRx is a pharma company, but it's also given rise to Hope Therapeutics , another healthcare services company that delivers effective treatments for mental health conditions—such as ketamine and transcranial magnetic stimulation —and, I imagine, more in the future.
statements.context: Speaker preview for Jonathan Javitt (NRx Pharmaceuticals). The author imagines Hope Therapeutics, NRx's care-delivery arm, will offer more treatments beyond ketamine and TMS in the future.
statements.note: Hedged, vague.

statements.quote: They made waves earlier this year, submitting an NDA for an on-label version of intravenous ketamine for depression to the FDA, and I imagine he's got more to say as well!
statements.context: Speaker preview for Jonathan Javitt: NRx submitted an NDA to the FDA for on-label IV ketamine (KetaFree) for depression; the author expects Javitt to have further news at RAMHT-AI.
statements.note: Low-stakes expectation about an event talk.

statements.quote: I've heard Josh has some big news for us, but we'll have to wait and see.
statements.context: Speaker preview for Josh Stevens, CEO of Beckley Clinical (infrastructure for ketamine-assisted therapy, brain stimulation and future psychedelic modalities). The author hints Beckley Clinical will announce big news at RAMHT-AI.
statements.note: Expectation about an event announcement.

statements.quote: Some of that is tools to make clinical workflows easier, and the underlying technology we're running clinical trials on right now at Radial may be the next wave in psychiatric diagnostic adjuvant technology.
statements.context: Speaker preview for Edwin Wong, CEO of Psyrin (vocal biomarker technology). Radial is running clinical trials on it; the author suggests it may become the next wave of psychiatric diagnostic adjuvant technology.
statements.note: Psyrin and Radial are the author's organizations; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: I have my own series of papers coming out with Jonathan as a co-author, and most importantly, he's a deeply gracious person.
statements.context: Speaker preview for Jonathan Downar (Ampa Health; Three-D trial; FDA-cleared TMS device; d-cycloserine augmentation; one-day TMS research). The author says he has a series of papers coming out with Downar as co-author.
statements.note: Own activity; low forecast value. CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: Having seen who has already bought tickets, I'm pretty sure that's likely to be the case.
statements.context: The author says the real goal is for audience members to be the most exciting part of RAMHT-AI, and given who has bought tickets he expects that to be true.
statements.note: Own-event expectation; low stakes. CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: Get ready for a night of big announcements, new technologies, new treatment models, innovative ways to think about business, innovative ways to think about patient care, and a focus on a future where people get better quickly, excessively, and safely from the brain disorders that once ailed them.
statements.context: Closing of the RAMHT-AI preview: the author predicts big announcements and new technologies will be presented at the event on Sunday January 11, 2026.
statements.note: Own-event promotion; CONTROL candidate.

statements.quote: It’s also worth reminding you all that RAMHT happens tomorrow night in San Fran!
statements.context: Podcast blurb (FINN Voices with host Erica) about trust in healthcare; reminder that RAMHT-AI takes place the next night (January 11, 2026) in San Francisco.
statements.note: Own-event reminder; CONTROL candidate.
